questions.question: Two bells are rung at intervals of 1,764 seconds and 2,268 seconds, respectively. They are rung together at the start. After how much time will the two bells ring together again for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find when the **bells ring together** again, calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the two time intervals.

Find the common factor: 1764 = 252 × 7 and 2268 = 252 × 9.

**LCM** = 252 × 7 × 9 = 252 × 63 = 15876 seconds.

Convert 15876 seconds: 15876 ÷ 3600 = 4 hours, remainder 1476; 1476 ÷ 60 = 24 minutes, remainder 36 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 24 min 36 sec.**

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 4 : 13 : 9, and their LCM is 6084. Their HCF is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the ratio parts are **pairwise coprime** (meaning no two parts share a common factor), the **LCM** is simply the **HCF × Product of Ratio Parts**.

Ratio parts 4, 13, and 9 are pairwise coprime.

⇒ 6084 = HCF × (4 × 13 × 9)

⇒ 6084 = HCF × 468

⇒ HCF = 6084 ÷ 468 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

questions.question: Pipes X, Y, and Z together can fill a tank in 8 hours. If all three work together for 3 hours, and then pipe Z is closed, the remaining tank is filled by X and Y in 10 hours. In how many hours can pipe Z alone fill the empty tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by **Pipes X, Y, and Z** in 3 hr = 3/8 part.

Remaining work = 1 − 3/8 = 5/8 part.

**X and Y** fill 5/8 part in 10 hr ⇒ full tank in 10 × 8/5 = 16 hr.

Efficiency of **pipe Z** = 1/8 − 1/16 = 1/16.

Time taken by **pipe Z** alone = 16 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (**X+Y+Z**) = 8 hr

Work done by (**X+Y+Z**) in 3 hr = 3/8

Remaining work = 1 − 3/8 = 5/8

Time taken by (**X+Y**) to fill 5/8 part = 10 hr

⇒ Time for (**X+Y**) to fill full tank = 10 × 8/5 = 16 hr

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days (hr)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **X+Y+Z**
 8
 16
 16 ÷ 8 = 2
 
 

 **X+Y**
 16
 16 ÷ 16 = 1
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of **pipe Z** = Efficiency of (**X+Y+Z**) − Efficiency of (**X+Y**)

⇒ Efficiency of **pipe Z** = 2 − 1 = 1

⇒ Time taken by **pipe Z** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Z

⇒ Time = 16 ÷ 1 = 16 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work, Time, and Efficiency Relationship

The total work is the product of efficiency and time (Work = Efficiency × Time). Efficiency is the amount of work done in a unit of time.

Combined Rate Rule

When multiple pipes work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ + E₃.

Inlet vs. Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes (filling) have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (emptying/leakage) have negative efficiency in calculation.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 27 and their product is 170. The positive difference between them is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify factors of the **product** 170 that add up to the **sum** 27.

170 = 17 × 10

Checking the sum: 17 + 10 = 27 (Satisfied)

Required **positive difference**: 17 − 10 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the two **positive numbers** be x and y.

**Given:** x + y = 27 and xy = 170

**Formula Used:** (x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fbfb5981c5be9211fb190baf2ecf2c2082ce25cb3dd4203d466943fc1bc0a1e.png] 

⇒ (x − y)² = (27)² − 4 × 170

⇒ (x − y)² = 729 − 680

⇒ (x − y)² = 49

⇒ x − y = √49

⇒ x − y = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity Relation

The relation between sum, difference, and product of two numbers is given by: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Quadratic Equation Formation

If the sum (S) and product (P) of two numbers are known, the numbers are the roots of the quadratic equation: t² − St + P = 0.

Sum of Squares

The sum of the squares of the numbers can be calculated as: x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy. In this case, 27² − 2(170) = 729 − 340 = 389.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is completely divisible by 6?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by **6** if it is both **even** (divisible by 2) and the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3.

Checking 7,53,216: It is **even** (ends in 6). Sum of digits = 7 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 6 = 24 (divisible by 3).

Checking other options: 5,47,821 is **odd**; 6,42,538 (sum=28) and 8,91,452 (sum=29) are **not divisible by 3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7,53,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Numbers:** 7,53,216, 6,42,538, 8,91,452, 5,47,821

A number is divisible by 6 if it satisfies two **divisibility rules** simultaneously:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e51ad4bc6d8c61ce8d5970fa996b5ac323410c56a3c5f96c5b71414b7a88eaaf.png] 

**Step-by-step verification for 7,53,216:**

⇒ **Condition 1 (Divisibility by 2):** The last digit is 6, which is even. ⇒ **Passed**.

⇒ **Condition 2 (Divisibility by 3):** Sum of digits = 7 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 6 = 24.

⇒ 24 ÷ 3 = 8 (No remainder). ⇒ **Passed**.

⇒ Since both conditions are satisfied, the number is divisible by 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 7,53,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 9

Similar to the rule for 3, a number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: A dealer sells a product at 15% profit. If he had bought it at 10% less and sold it for ₹126 less, he would have gained 20%. Find the cost price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial **Cost Price** = 100 units

Initial SP = 115 units and New CP = 90 units (10% less)

New SP = 90 × 120% = 108 units (20% gain)

Difference in SP = 115 − 108 = 7 units

7 units = ₹126 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹18 ⇒ 100 units = ₹1,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Profit = 15%, Reduction in CP = 10%, Reduction in SP = ₹126, New Profit = 20%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d07b370c9348c0b54fe8c3c093432ea88e22ec849ff9e3746b59117b47627d0b.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the product be ₹ x

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = x + 15% of x = 1.15x

⇒ New Cost Price (CP₂) = x − 10% of x = 0.90x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 0.90x + 20% of 0.90x

⇒ SP₂ = 0.90x × (120/100) = 1.08x

⇒ According to the question: SP₁ − SP₂ = 126

⇒ 1.15x − 1.08x = 126

⇒ 0.07x = 126

⇒ x = 126 ÷ 0.07

⇒ x = 12600 ÷ 7 = 1800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Net Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Relationship between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This is used for problems involving markup and discount.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 16% and 29% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 4%, 34% and 37% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 12% discount on the first 4 toys and 27% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 4 toys free of cost on buying 10 toys.

A customer wants to buy 10 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the **effective discount percentage** for each scheme on 10 toys:

(A) 16 + 29 − (16 × 29)/100 = 45 − 4.64 = **40.36%**

(B) Effective of (4, 34, 37) is approx. **60.1%** (high discount)

(C) Average discount = [(4 × 12%) + (6 × 27%)] ÷ 10 = (48 + 162) ÷ 10 = **21%**

(D) Discount = [Free ÷ Total] × 100 = (4 ÷ 14) × 100 ≈ **28.57%**

The **least beneficial** scheme is the one with the **lowest discount percentage**.

**∴ The correct answer is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total toys to buy = 10. Let **Marked Price (MP)** of 1 toy = ₹100. Total MP = ₹1000.

**Formula Used:** Effective Discount = (Total Discount ÷ Total MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e702d8a785f3c4b286e4041ee23c639f9d56ac1b5dcd5fd3c1102342d53d85e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

**Scheme (A):** Successive 16% and 29%

⇒ Net Discount = 16 + 29 − (16 × 29)/100 = 45 − 4.64 = 40.36%

**Scheme (B):** Successive 4%, 34% and 37%

⇒ First two: 4 + 34 − (4 × 34)/100 = 36.64%

⇒ Final: 36.64 + 37 − (36.64 × 37)/100 = 73.64 − 13.55 = 60.09%

**Scheme (C):** 12% on 4 toys and 27% on 6 toys

⇒ Discount on 4 toys = 4 × 12 = ₹48

⇒ Discount on 6 toys = 6 × 27 = ₹162

⇒ Total Discount = 48 + 162 = ₹210

⇒ Effective Discount % = (210 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 21%

**Scheme (D):** 4 toys free on buying 10 toys

⇒ Effective Discount % = [Free ÷ (Paid + Free)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = [4 ÷ (10 + 4)] × 100 = 400 ÷ 14 ≈ 28.57%

Comparing all, **Scheme C** offers the **minimum discount (21%)**, making it the **least beneficial** for the customer.

**∴ The correct answer is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (ab/100)]%.

Buy X Get Y Free

In such schemes, the effective discount percentage is calculated as [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Customer's Benefit

A scheme is **most beneficial** when the **discount is maximum** and **least beneficial** when the **discount is minimum**.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 5. If 6 is subtracted from each, the resulting numbers are in the ratio 1 : 2. Find the difference between the two original numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **Ratio** = 3 : 5 (Difference = 2 units)

Final **Ratio** = 1 : 2 (Difference = 1 unit)

Equating the difference by multiplying the final ratio by 2: 1 × 2 : 2 × 2 = 2 : 4

Comparison: 3 → 2 and 5 → 4 (Decrease of 1 unit = 6)

Original **Difference** = 5 − 3 = 2 units ⇒ 2 × 6 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Ratio** of numbers = 3 : 5

Value **subtracted** from each = 6

Resulting **Ratio** = 1 : 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c851f84b88c2fcb49187f3437f250f8afa6800f005267bdceb40f9b6b17cfdea.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If ratio is a : b, numbers are ax and bx. Difference = (b − a)x

**Calculations:**

Let the two numbers be 3x and 5x.

⇒ (3x − 6) / (5x − 6) = 1 / 2

⇒ 2 × (3x − 6) = 1 × (5x − 6)

⇒ 6x − 12 = 5x − 6

⇒ 6x − 5x = 12 − 6

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Original **Difference** = 5x − 3x = 2x

⇒ 2 × 6 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Difference Property

When the same quantity is added to or subtracted from both terms of a **ratio**, the absolute difference between the terms remains a constant multiple of the common variable x.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For any ratio problem involving changes, the **Cross-product** method (Product of extremes = Product of means) is the most reliable way to set up the linear equation.

Proportionality

A **proportion** is an equality of two ratios. If a/b = c/d, then a × d = b × c.

questions.question:
Find the diameter of a sphere of surface area 28962 cm². (round off to the closest integer)

(Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area of a **sphere** in terms of **diameter** (d) is π × d².

28962 ≈ (22/7) × d²

d² ≈ (28962 × 7) ÷ 22 ≈ 9215.18

Since 96² = 9216, the **diameter** d ≈ 96 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Surface Area (SA) of the **sphere** = 28962 cm²

Value of π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of **sphere** = 4 × π × r²

**Diameter** (d) = 2 × r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84a998ee7bce68f83184da897167b85932d8ff433325f476b0c224d79a0d51c9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × r²

⇒ 28962 = (88/7) × r²

⇒ r² = (28962 × 7) ÷ 88

⇒ r² = 202734 ÷ 88

⇒ r² = 2303.795

⇒ r = √2303.795 ≈ 47.997

⇒ **Diameter** (d) = 2 × r

⇒ d = 2 × 47.997 = 95.994

⇒ Rounding to the **closest integer**, d ≈ 96 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume (V) of a sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Hemisphere Surface Area

For a solid **hemisphere**, Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr² and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr².

Circle vs Sphere

A circle is a 2D shape with **area** πr², while a sphere is its 3D counterpart with **surface area** 4πr².

questions.question: Simplify the following expression using the BODMAS rule: (3)/(4) + ((5)/(6) times (9)/(10)) - (2)/(3)

questions.question: If a two-digit number has a digit sum of 9 and adding 27 reverses its digits, determine the unit digit of the number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **two-digit number**, the difference between its digits is equal to the change in value upon **reversing digits** divided by 9.

Difference between digits = 27 ÷ 9 = 3

Given **digit sum** = 9

Unit digit = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (9 + 3) ÷ 2 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of digits of a **two-digit number** = 9

Number + 27 = Reversed Number

**Method:** Algebraic representation where tens digit is x and **unit digit** is y.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6deab024ec54f8e255f51529f5bf9d01bd517b781fe8a2b500059afc06702e8f.png] 

Let the tens digit be x and the unit digit be y.

⇒ x + y = 9 ... (i)

⇒ The original number is 10x + y.

⇒ According to the problem: (10x + y) + 27 = 10y + x

⇒ 10x − x + y − 10y = −27

⇒ 9x − 9y = −27

⇒ x − y = −3 or y − x = 3 ... (ii)

⇒ Adding equation (i) and (ii): (x + y) + (y − x) = 9 + 3

⇒ 2y = 12

⇒ y = 6

⇒ x = 9 − 6 = 3

The number is 36 and its **unit digit** is 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number Representation

A two-digit number with tens digit x and unit digit y is expressed as 10x + y. Its reversed form is 10y + x.

Difference Property

The difference between any two-digit number and its reverse is always a multiple of 9, specifically 9 × |x − y|.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

questions.question: Extended ASCII, an 8-bit evolution of the original 7-bit ASCII standard, supports international text by expanding the character set. How many total codes does it provide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**256 codes including accented characters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Extended ASCII** is an **8-bit** character encoding scheme that doubles the capacity of the original **7-bit Standard ASCII**.
 
• The number of unique codes in a binary system is calculated as 2ⁿ, where n is the number of bits. For an **8-bit system**, this results in **2⁸ = 256** unique character representations.
 
• The original **ASCII** set occupies the first **128 positions** (0 to 127), which include English letters, digits, and control characters.
 
• The additional **128 positions** (128 to 255) provided by the **Extended ASCII** set are used to map **accented characters** (such as á, é, ñ), mathematical symbols, and box-drawing glyphs.
 
• This expansion was critical for supporting **Western European languages** and other international symbols that could not be represented within the original 7-bit constraint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Encoding Standards**:

 
 
• **Standard ASCII**: Developed in **1963**, it only utilized 7 bits, allowing for **128 codes**, which was sufficient for basic English but lacked international support.
 
• **ISO 8859-1**: Also known as **Latin-1**, this is one of the most common implementations of **Extended ASCII**, catering specifically to Western European alphabets.
 
• **Unicode**: To solve the limitations of the **256-code** ceiling, **Unicode** (such as **UTF-8**) was introduced, which can represent over **1.1 million characters** across all global languages.
 
 
 
• **Data Representation**:
 
 
• In **7-bit ASCII**, the eighth bit of a **byte** was often used as a **parity bit** for error detection during data transmission.
 
• In **Extended ASCII**, the eighth bit is repurposed as a data bit to expand the addressable character space to **256**.

questions.question: How does increasing the Amplitude of a sound wave affect the sound produced?

options.text: The speed of the sound increases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The loudness increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amplitude** represents the maximum displacement of the particles of a medium from their mean equilibrium position when a **sound wave** passes through it.
 
• The **loudness** of a sound is a physical sensation that depends directly on the **amplitude** of the vibrating object; specifically, **loudness** is proportional to the square of the **amplitude** (Loudness ∝ Amplitude²).
 
• When the **amplitude** of the vibration is increased, the **energy** carried by the sound wave increases, which the human ear perceives as an increase in **volume** or **loudness**.
 
• If the **amplitude** is doubled, the **loudness** becomes four times (2²) greater, whereas if the **amplitude** is tripled, the **loudness** increases by nine times (3²).
 
• **Loudness** is typically measured in units called **decibels (dB)**, and it serves to distinguish between a **faint** sound and a **loud** sound produced by the same source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitch and Frequency**:

 
 
• **Pitch** is the characteristic of sound that allows us to distinguish between a **shrill** sound and a **grave** (deep) sound.
 
• It depends entirely on the **frequency** of the sound wave (the number of vibrations per second), not the **amplitude**.
 
• Higher **frequency** results in a higher **pitch**, while lower **frequency** results in a lower **pitch**.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound**:
 
 
• The **velocity** of sound is determined by the properties of the **medium**, such as **elasticity**, **density**, **temperature**, and **humidity**.
 
• Altering the **amplitude** or **frequency** of the wave does not change the **speed** at which the sound travels through a uniform medium.
 
 
 
• **Timbre (Quality)**:
 
 
• This is the property that enables us to differentiate between sounds of the same **loudness** and **pitch** produced by different instruments, determined by the **wave shape**.

questions.question: Which of the following belts of the Northern Plains consists of porous rocky soil where stream water seeps underground?

• The **Bhabar belt** is a narrow region situated immediately at the foothills of the **Shiwalik Range**, marking the northernmost boundary of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**.
 
• This belt stretches from the **Indus River** in the west to the **Teesta River** in the east, maintaining a width of approximately **8 to 16 kilometers**.
 
• It is primarily composed of **pebbles**, **gravel**, and **heavy boulders** deposited by **Himalayan rivers** as they descend from the mountains and lose their velocity.
 
• The accumulation of these coarse materials results in extremely high **porosity** and permeability of the soil, causing surface streams to **seep underground** and disappear from the surface.
 
• Due to the lack of surface water and the presence of un-sorted rocky debris, this belt is generally **unsuitable for agriculture**, though large trees with deep roots can survive.
 
• Therefore, the **Bhabar belt** is the correct option.

questions.question: Which of the following optical properties of light enables sunglasses to reduce glare from sunlight reflected off surfaces such as water or roads?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polarization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Polarization** is the process by which the vibrations of a **transverse wave**, such as light, are restricted to a single plane of direction. Natural sunlight is **unpolarized**, meaning its waves vibrate in multiple planes perpendicular to its path of travel.
 
• When light strikes a non-metallic horizontal surface like **water** or a **wet road**, it undergoes reflection. This reflected light becomes **horizontally polarized**, meaning the light waves predominantly vibrate in a horizontal orientation parallel to the surface.
 
• The intense, concentrated light resulting from this horizontal reflection is what we identify as **glare**. It is often blinding and reduces visual contrast, making it difficult to see objects clearly.
 
• **Polarized sunglasses** are designed with a special chemical film containing molecules aligned in **vertical rows**. This structure creates a **vertical transmission axis** that allows only vertically vibrating light to pass through while absorbing or blocking the horizontal component.
 
• By filtering out the **horizontal light waves**, these lenses effectively eliminate the glare from surfaces, allowing the wearer to see into the water or view the road with much higher **definition and safety**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interference**:

 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when two or more light waves overlap to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same **amplitude**.
 
• In optics, **thin-film interference** is utilized in **anti-reflective (AR) coatings** for eyeglasses to reduce surface reflections, but it does not selectively filter polarized glare.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**:
 
 
• This refers to the **bending of light** as it passes around the edge of an object or through a narrow aperture.
 
• It is a fundamental principle in **spectroscopy** and the study of the **wave nature of light**, but it is unrelated to the functionality of glare-reducing sunglasses.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**:
 
 
• This is the change in **direction and speed** of light as it passes from one medium to another, such as from **air into glass**.
 
• While **refraction** is the core principle used to create **corrective lenses** (to fix nearsightedness or farsightedness), it does not account for the removal of reflected glare.
 
 
 
• **Brewster's Law**:
 
 
• This law states that maximum polarization occurs when the **tangent** of the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **refractive index** of the reflecting medium.

• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a summary composite measure of average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living.

• The **Poverty line ratio**, which indicates the percentage of the population living below a specific income threshold, is not a constituent indicator of the **HDI**. It is instead used in other metrics like the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** or national poverty assessments.

questions.question: During the electrolysis of water, hydrogen and oxygen are released in which ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2:1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolysis** is the process of using **electricity** to decompose a compound into its constituent elements. In the case of **water** (H₂O), it is split into **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen** gases.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for the electrolysis of water is **2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)**.
 
• According to the **stoichiometry** of this reaction, two molecules of water decompose to produce **two molecules of Hydrogen** gas and **one molecule of Oxygen** gas.
 
• Based on **Avogadro Law**, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles of the gas at a constant temperature and pressure. Therefore, the **molar ratio** of 2:1 translates directly to a **volume ratio** of 2:1.
 
• During the **electrolytic decomposition**, the amount of hydrogen gas collected is exactly double the amount of oxygen gas by volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrode Reactions**:

 
 
• At the **Cathode** (negative electrode), **reduction** takes place: 4H⁺ + 4e− → 2H₂(g). This is where **Hydrogen gas** is released.
 
• At the **Anode** (positive electrode), **oxidation** takes place: 2H₂O → O₂(g) + 4H⁺ + 4e−. This is where **Oxygen gas** is released.
 
 
 
• **Mass Ratio**: It is important to distinguish between volume and mass. The **mass ratio** of Hydrogen to Oxygen in water is **1:8**, because oxygen is significantly denser and heavier than hydrogen.
 
• **Electrolyte**: Pure water is a **poor conductor** of electricity. To facilitate electrolysis, a few drops of **dilute Sulphuric acid** (H₂SO₄) or a salt are added to provide free ions for conductivity.
 
• **Hofmann Voltameter**: This is the specialized apparatus used to perform this experiment, allowing for the visual verification of the **2:1 displacement ratio** in the gas collection tubes.

questions.question:
Which statement is True or False about the Windows 11 Operating System (OS)?

(i) The OS loads program code directly onto the hard disk for execution, as the CPU can only execute code from permanent storage.

(ii) For multitasking, the OS allocates small CPU time slices to processes, rapidly switching between them, a technique known as Time-Sharing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) False, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** does not execute program code directly from a **Hard Disk** or any permanent storage device because these devices are significantly slower than the processor; instead, the **Operating System (OS)** must first load the code into the **Random Access Memory (RAM)** for execution. Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.
 
• **Windows 11** utilizes a **Preemptive Multitasking** model where the **OS Scheduler** assigns a specific duration of processor time, known as a **Time Slice** or **Quantum**, to various active processes, switching between them so rapidly that it creates the effect of simultaneous execution. Hence, statement (ii) is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Random Access Memory (RAM):**

 
 
• It is the **Primary Memory** of the computer system characterized by high-speed data access and **Volatile** storage, meaning it loses data when power is removed.
 
• The **Memory Management** unit of the **Windows 11 OS** ensures that only the necessary fragments of a program (pages) are loaded into **RAM** to optimize performance.
 
 
 
• **Time-Sharing Systems:**
 
 
• This technique allows multiple users or programs to share the resources of a single **CPU** by alternating execution in small intervals, improving **Throughput** and responsiveness.
 
• It prevents a single application from monopolizing the **Processor**, ensuring a smooth **User Interface (UI)** experience in modern environments like **Windows 11**.
 
 
 
• **Windows 11 OS Architecture:**
 
 
• It is built upon the **Windows NT** kernel, which is designed to handle complex **Process Scheduling**, security protocols, and **Virtual Memory** management.
 
• The system uses **Context Switching** to save the state of a process before moving to the next time slice, allowing the previous task to resume exactly where it left off.

• A crucial step in this restoration was the removal of the **Right to Property** as a **Fundamental Right** (originally **Article 19(1)(f)** and **Article 31**) and its reclassification as a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**, which reduced the friction between state-led socio-economic reforms and individual rights.
 
• The amendment also ensured that the enforcement of the rights guaranteed by **Articles 20 and 21** (Protection in respect of conviction for offences and Protection of life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even during a **National Emergency**.

questions.question: When did Ladakh become a union territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ladakh** officially became a **Union Territory** of India on **October 31, 2019**, following the enactment of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• The proposal to reorganize the state was introduced in the **Rajya Sabha** on **August 5, 2019**, and received the **Presidential assent** on **August 9, 2019**.
 
• This administrative change led to the **bifurcation** of the erstwhile state of **Jammu and Kashmir** into two separate Union Territories: **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
 
• The effective date, **October 31**, was chosen to coincide with the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who played a pivotal role in the political integration of India.
 
• **Ladakh** is established as a Union Territory **without a legislature**, meaning it is governed directly by the **Central Government** through an appointed **Lieutenant Governor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Structure of Ladakh**:

 
 
• The Union Territory comprises two primary districts: **Leh** and **Kargil**.
 
• **Radha Krishna Mathur** was sworn in as the first **Lieutenant Governor** of the Union Territory of Ladakh in 2019.
 
• While it lacks a state-level assembly, it retains its **Autonomous Hill Development Councils** for both Leh and Kargil to manage local governance.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Context**:
 
 
• The transition occurred alongside the effective **abrogation of Article 370**, which previously granted special autonomous status to the region.
 
• The **Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir**, unlike Ladakh, was created with a provision for its own **Legislative Assembly**, similar to the model of Puducherry.
 
• **National Unity Day** (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is celebrated annually on **October 31**, the same day the new administrative status of the region was formalized.

questions.question: Which of the following sites contains prehistoric paintings ranging from the Mesolithic to the historic period?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Located in the **Raisen district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, the **Bhimbetka rock shelters** are situated within the **Vindhya Mountain Range** and represent the earliest traces of human life on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The site features over **700 rock shelters**, containing paintings that provide a continuous cultural record from the **Upper Paleolithic** and **Mesolithic** periods through the **Chalcolithic** and into the **historic period**.
 
• **Mesolithic paintings** at Bhimbetka are characterized by depictions of hunting, dancing, and various animals such as **bison**, **tigers**, and **elephants**, often painted in **red and white** pigments.
 
• The **historic period paintings** at the site demonstrate a transition in social life, featuring **warriors** on horseback, **processions**, and **religious symbols**, indicating more organized societal structures.
 
• Discovered by archaeologist **Dr. V.S. Wakankar** in **1957**, Bhimbetka was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2003** for its exceptional prehistoric art.

• Situated in **Bihar**, it was a world-famous ancient **Buddhist university** and monastic center that reached its peak during the **Gupta Empire** and **Pala Empire**.
 
• It is purely a **historic period** site, serving as a hub for higher learning and Buddhist philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Hampi**:
 
 
• Located in **Karnataka** on the banks of the **Tungabhadra River**, it was the grand capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** during the 14th to 16th centuries.
 
• It is known for its **Dravidian style** temple architecture and was a major **medieval historic** trade center.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal**:
 
 
• A **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **Karnataka**, it represents the high point of **Chalukya architecture** during the 7th and 8th centuries.
 
• The site features a unique blend of **Nagara** and **Dravidian** temple styles, categorized as the **Vesara style**, and belongs strictly to the **historic period**.

questions.question: Uvx ranked 14th from the top and 79th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Total number of students = (Rank from the top + Rank from the bottom) − 1

**Given:**

**Rank of Uvx from the top** = 14th

**Rank of Uvx from the bottom** = 79th

**Total number of students** = (Rank from the top + Rank from the bottom) − 1

= (14 + 79) − 1

= 93 − 1

= 92

Hence, the **total number of students** in the class is 92.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 2'**.
